formula: slope = atan(hypot(dz/dx, dz/dy)); central differences; dy = R*dlat = 1895.2 m; dx = dy*cos(lat) (one pixel east-west, true metric spacing, periodic in longitude); across the pole the neighbour is the same-latitude pixel at longitude+180

formula: temp_k = mean over the 96 local-time bins of the diurnal tbol curve, after circular linear interpolation of empty bins (gaps of at most 12 bins = 3 h); labelled DERIVED, not MEASURED, because of that gap filling

product: LOLA average solar illumination AVGVISIB_65S/65N_240M_201608 (Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211:1066)
licence_credit: NASA PDS data: publicly released, no access restrictions; NASA-produced data are not subject to US copyright (licence string not stated on the product page). Credit: LOLA team / NASA GSFC PGDA (E. Mazarico); Mazarico et al. 2011
native_resolution: 240 m polar stereographic (sphere 1737.4 km), 65-90 deg N and S
aggregation: mean of all 240 m pixels whose centre falls in the cell (polar-stereographic -> lat/lon by the spherical formula rho = 2R tan((90-|lat|)/2)); only rows with |centre lat| >= 65.5
formula: DERIVED_LOLA_TOPOGRAPHY: label 'percentage of timesteps where each pixel was sunlit (by any fraction of the solar disc)', hourly over ~18.6 yr, computed by the LOLA team by ray tracing over LOLA topography (a simulation from measured topography, not a measurement of light). DERIVED_FLAT_GEOMETRY (|lat| < 65): fraction of time the upper limb of the Sun is above a flat horizon, obliquity 1.54 deg, semi-diameter 0.2666 deg, year-averaged (see sun formula)
caveats: Height above ground: the label states none; computed for the surface (0 m). Published values at 2 m and 10 m (Glaser et al. 2014) are higher. The DERIVED values ignore topographic shadowing (flat ground). A 1 deg cell (~30 km) averages lit ridges with shadowed craters: the best sites (~0.9) do not appear at this resolution. At |lat| = 65 the value jumps from ~0.50 (flat geometry) to ~0.44 (LOLA topography, with topographic shadowing): the jump is the shadowing the flat-ground formula ignores, not an error.

product: solar constant (NSSDC Moon fact sheet) + exact geometry; LOLA topographic illum_frac where it exists (|lat| >= 65.5)
licence_credit: NASA NSSDC fact sheet; NASA Photojournal PIA13720
aggregation: none
formula: Horizontal surface, no atmosphere, Sun-Moon distance 1 au, per 24-hour Earth day. Geometric: Q = S0 * <max(0, sin h)> * 24/1000, S0 = 1361.0 W/m2, sin h = sin(lat) sin(d) + cos(lat) cos(d) cos(H), sin d = sin(eps) sin(L), time mean over H and L uniform. Where the LOLA topographic illum_frac exists: Q = S0 * illum_frac * <sin h | h > 0> * 24/1000 (the topographic lit fraction replaces the geometric daylight fraction; multiplying the geometric Q by illum_frac would count the night twice). Results (cell centres): 0.5 deg (equator) 10.40, 45.5 deg 7.29, 85.5 deg 0.840 kWh/m2/day (geometric); 85.5 deg with the median topographic illum_frac of that row 0.247: 0.415 kWh/m2/day (<sin h | h>0> at 85.5 deg = 0.0514)
caveats: Horizontal panel. A vertical sun-tracking panel at the pole receives ~S0 whenever lit (about 32.7 kWh/m2 per 24 h at illum_frac 1); the engine's thresholds were written for horizontal Earth irradiance. Lunar day = 29.53 Earth days, so 'per day' is a long-run mean.

aggregation: none
formula: (time with 0 < h < 5 deg) / (time with h > 0), year average; quadrature on 720 seasons x 2880 hour angles; sin h as for irradiance; Sun centre, no refraction
caveats: Equals 1 poleward of ~85 deg (the Sun never exceeds 5 deg).
